project.name: IAPGuard AI
project.description: Educational full-stack prototype for detecting unusual synthetic in-app purchase behavior with a PyTorch variational autoencoder and presenting investigations in a React dashboard.

nodes.name: .env.example
nodes.summary: Optional environment configuration template for overriding the backend data directory and frontend API base URL.
nodes.languageNotes: Configuration template with commented shell-style environment variable assignments.

nodes.name: CODEX.md
nodes.summary: Contributor guidance for running, testing, and extending the educational fraud anomaly-detection prototype while keeping data synthetic and avoiding production fraud claims.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown instructions and repository-specific development notes.

nodes.name: README.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive project documentation covering the IAPGuard AI prototype, its React and FastAPI stack, VAE anomaly-detection pipeline, local setup, API endpoints, scoring behavior, and production limitations.
nodes.languageNotes: Markdown user and developer documentation with tables, diagrams, shell commands, and JSON examples.

nodes.name: start-frontend.bat

nodes.name: start-frontend.sh
nodes.summary: Unix shell script that enters the frontend directory, installs npm dependencies when needed, and launches the Vite development server.
nodes.languageNotes: POSIX-style shell script invoking npm install and npm run dev.

nodes.name: model.py

nodes.name: synthetic.py

nodes.name: api.js

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Begin with the README to understand IAPGuard AI as an educational, synthetic-data prototype: a React dashboard over a FastAPI service that uses a PyTorch variational autoencoder to identify unusual in-app purchase behavior. Review the documented architecture, local setup, API surface, and safety limitations before exploring implementation details.

tour.title: Backend API and Application Lifecycle
tour.description: Follow the FastAPI application in main.py from lifespan startup through database initialization, model loading or training, synthetic seeding, and rescoring. Then trace the health, overview, transaction, review, analysis, model, retraining, reset, and evaluation endpoints, including the Pydantic request validation and demo-only behavior.

tour.title: Persistence and Synthetic Data
tour.description: Study db.py to see how the SQLite data directory is configured, connections commit or roll back, tables and indexes are created, and transactions and reviews are stored. Compare that schema with synthetic.py, which produces reproducible normal records and injected anomaly patterns for the seeded demo and evaluation metrics.

tour.title: VAE Anomaly Detection
tour.description: Trace model.py's eleven engineered features, scaling, encoder and decoder, latent sampling during training, deterministic inference, reconstruction-error scoring, residual ranking, percentile calibration, and local checkpoint persistence. Connect these mechanics to the API's risk levels and the dashboard's interpretation that anomaly scores are not fraud probabilities or causal explanations.

tour.title: Frontend Dashboard and API Integration
tour.description: Start at the Vite HTML entry point and main.jsx to learn the single-page navigation, overview metrics and charts, transaction explorer, alert queue, detection lab, model insights, and review drawer. Then read api.js for the shared REST wrapper, error handling, formatting helpers, and configurable API base URL; finish with the Vite proxy and responsive styling.

tour.title: Backend Integration Tests
tour.description: Use the pytest configuration and test_api.py as an executable tour of the backend contract. The end-to-end test isolates its database and model directory, verifies startup and readiness, exercises overview, filtering, details, reviews, manual analysis, evaluation, and model endpoints, and confirms the not-found path.

tour.title: Startup and Development Tooling
tour.description: Finish by comparing the Windows batch and Unix shell launchers. Each backend script creates or activates a virtual environment, installs requirements, and runs Uvicorn; each frontend script installs npm dependencies when needed and starts Vite. Use the README commands and environment template to understand ports, proxy behavior, and optional configuration overrides.
